reason: E3 and E1 show that W-containing BCC refractory HEAs (MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) retain strength well at high temperature, supporting the premise that W can improve high-temperature strength retention. However, E4 shows that W addition in a different BCC HEA system led to Laves phase formation and sharp ductility loss, directly conflicting with the premise that ductility will be only modestly compromised. The cited evidence does not provide specific support for the claim that W addition to TiVNbTa will maintain acceptable ductility, nor does it quantify the predicted 30–50% strength improvement.
premises: W addition to BCC TiVNbTa will enhance solid-solution strengthening at high temperature
W addition will improve high-temperature yield strength retention relative to the TiVNbTa baseline
W addition will maintain acceptable ductility (only a modest compromise)
The strengthening mechanism is increased resistance to dislocation motion from W-induced lattice distortions
The baseline TiVNbTa has ~330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K
